## Lyrics (public domain)

Public domain in the US: words published in 1930 or earlier. Each song's verses were copied from the source linked below: a Wikisource page, or, where marked, a Wikipedia article that quotes the original text of that year. Only 1 to 3 verses of each song are kept. Recordings and later arrangements are not used. The Batman playground parody of Jingle Bells (1960s) is not public domain, so none of its lines are stored; it appears only as a description.

- Amazing Grace (1779): https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Olney_Hymns_(1840)/Book_1/Hymn_41
- Danny Boy (1913): https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Danny_Boy
- Go Down, Moses (1872): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_Down_Moses (copied from this Wikipedia article, which quotes the 1872 text)
- Take Me Out to the Ball Game (1908): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_Me_Out_to_the_Ball_Game (copied from this Wikipedia article, which quotes the 1908 text)
- Yes! We Have No Bananas (1923): https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Yes!_We_Have_No_Bananas

## Genre, mood and energy values

`data/library/songs.json` gives each song four values. `genre_label` is the song's real genre, copied from the Wikipedia infobox or article intro where one was found (`genre_label_source` says which) and otherwise an estimate. `genre` is only the nearest word in the 16-word vocabulary of `data/songs.csv`, so the Project 3 scorer can use it; it is a mapping, not a claim about the song. `mood` and `energy` (0 to 1) are estimates with no source: proposed by the build session (Claude) on Nov 17, 2026 and kept by Danny on Nov 18, 2026.
